Students will be able to independently use their learning to…

	UNDERSTANDING
Students will understand that…
The inverse relationship between addition and subtraction. Place value strategies and base ten models to add and subtract whole numbers. Rounding numbers can be useful when estimating. Solve problems with a variety of unknowns (start, change, result, etc.).
	ESSENTIAL QUESTIONS
Students will keep considering…
How can I read, write, compare, and order numbers to the ten-thousand place? How can I determine the place and value of digits within a given number? 	ACQUISITION — Students will KNOW…
Knowing how to round will help you with addition and subtraction. You can use what you know about place value to add or subtract using partial sums or differences and other strategies. How the place of a number determines its value. Knowing how to compare and round numbers to the nearest 10 or 100. Using estimation to check the reasonableness of solutions. Knowing basic addition and subtraction facts to add/subtract multi-digit whole numbers up to 10,000.

	TRANSFER
Students will be able to independently use their learning to…
Multiply and divide facts up through 10. Explain multiplication as combining multiple groups. Use multiple strategies and representations to model multiplication and division. Relate multiplication to division. Multiply single-digit factors by multiples of 10. Solve multiplication and division problems with unknown factors in all positions. Find and explain patterns.
	UNDERSTANDING
Students will understand that…
Multiplication is a way of combining equal groups. There are many models and strategies to help you multiply. You can multiply numbers in any order. Division means separating a total number of objects into equal-size groups. Properties of multiplication (commutative, associative, distributive). The inverse relationship between multiplication and division. The connection between multiplication and division fact families. Place value strategies to multiply by multiples of 10.
	ESSENTIAL QUESTIONS
Students will keep considering…
How can I use models to explain the meaning of multiplication? How can I multiply by factors 0, 1, 2, 5, and 10? How can I multiply by factors 3, 4, and 6? How can I multiply by factors 7, 8, and 9? How can I use the commutative and associative properties to multiply whole numbers? How can I explain the relationship between multiplication and division? How can I use patterns to help understand addition and multiplication facts?
	ACQUISITION — Students will KNOW…
Knowing how to work with equal groups will help with both multiplication and division. Breaking apart factors will help with fluency. The commutative, associative, distributive, and identity properties of multiplication. Inverse relationship between multiplication and division. How to find the rule for a numerical pattern and explain it. How to use place value to multiply. Models: groups of, sets of, arrays.
	ACQUISITION — Students will be SKILLED AT…
Explain multiplication using equal groups and arrays. Break apart numbers to make multiplying easier (e.g., 3×8=(3×4)+(3×4)). Use order and grouping to make multiplying easier (e.g., 2×6×5=6×(2×5)). Use place value to multiply (e.g., 3×40=3×4×10). Explain division using equal groups and arrays. Understand how multiplication and division are related. Students will be able to independently use their learning to…
Determine the place and value of a given digit within whole numbers. Read and write whole numbers up to 10,000. Compare and order whole numbers up to 10,000. Round whole numbers within 1,000 to the nearest 10 and 100. Add and subtract whole numbers up to 10,000.
	UNDERSTANDING
Students will understand that…
The inverse relationship between addition and subtraction. Place value strategies and base ten models to add and subtract whole numbers. The position of a digit within a given number determines the value of that digit. Place value strategies and base ten models to compare and order whole numbers. Rounding numbers can be useful when estimating. Solve problems with a variety of unknowns (start, change, result, etc.).
	ESSENTIAL QUESTIONS
Students will keep considering…
How can I read, write, compare, and order numbers to the ten-thousand place? How can I determine the place and value of digits within a given number? 	ACQUISITION — Students will KNOW…
Knowing how to round will help you with addition and subtraction. You can use what you know about place value to add or subtract using partial sums or differences and other strategies. Knowing basic addition and subtraction facts to add/subtract multi-digit whole numbers up to 10,000.

UNIT 2 — Multiplication and Division: Concepts, Relationships, and Patterns
Sept 8 – Nov 7, 2026  |  39 days  |  Standards: 3.PAR.3.1, 3.PAR.3.3, 3.PAR.3.4, 3.PAR.3.5, 3.PAR.3.6, 3.PAR.3.7
	 
STAGE 1: DESIRED RESULTS
	ESTABLISHED GOALS
Standards: 3.PAR.3.1, 3.PAR.3.3, 3.PAR.3.4, 3.PAR.3.5, 3.PAR.3.6, 3.PAR.3.7
Vocabulary: Arrange, Array, Equation, Expression, Factor, Multiplication, Multiply, Product, Break Apart, Associative Property, Commutative Property, Pack, Divide, Dividend, Division, Divisor, Model, Partition, Quotient, Fact Family, Even/Odd Number, Multiplication Table, Pattern, Rule
	TRANSFER
Students will be able to independently use their learning to…
Multiply and divide facts up through 10. Explain multiplication as combining multiple groups. Use multiple strategies and representations to model multiplication and division. Relate multiplication to division. Multiply single-digit factors by multiples of 10. Solve multiplication and division problems with unknown factors in all positions. Find and explain patterns.
	UNDERSTANDING
Students will understand that…
Multiplication is a way of combining equal groups. There are many models and strategies to help you multiply. You can multiply numbers in any order. Division means separating a total number of objects into equal-size groups. Properties of multiplication (commutative, associative, distributive). The inverse relationship between multiplication and division. The connection between multiplication and division fact families. Place value strategies to multiply by multiples of 10.
	ESSENTIAL QUESTIONS
Students will keep considering…
How can I use models to explain the meaning of multiplication? How can I multiply by factors 0, 1, 2, 5, and 10? How can I multiply by factors 3, 4, and 6? How can I multiply by factors 7, 8, and 9? How can I use the commutative and associative properties to multiply whole numbers? How can I explain the relationship between multiplication and division? How can I use patterns to help understand addition and multiplication facts?
	ACQUISITION — Students will KNOW…
Knowing how to work with equal groups will help with both multiplication and division. Breaking apart factors will help with fluency. The commutative, associative, distributive, and identity properties of multiplication. Inverse relationship between multiplication and division. How to find the rule for a numerical pattern and explain it. How to use place value to multiply. Models: groups of, sets of, arrays.
